Family Therapy

Family Therapy helps families resolve current problems, improve communication, and build a more supportive home environment. Therapy focuses on practical strategies for conflict resolution, boundary setting, parenting consistency, and rebuilding connection so families can function more calmly and cooperatively. Michelle Barratt Psychology (MBP) provides in-person therapy to families across Brisbane, and flexible online therapy options Australia-wide, ensuring that family support is always accessible.

How does MBP support therapy for Family Therapy?

Michelle Barratt Psychology Administrative Services (MBP) provides a clinically informed administrative hub that removes logistical barriers for families seeking care from Brisbane psychologists and allied health practitioners . We manage complex scheduling, multi-party communications, and referral coordination so independent clinicians can devote their full attention to therapeutic work.

What does MBP look after for your family?

Coordinated Scheduling

Appointment scheduling is organised across family members to minimise delays, missed appointments, and administrative complexity.

Sensitive Intake

A clinically informed intake and triage process helps connect your family with the most appropriate practitioner.

Confidential Communication

Professional communication is managed discreetly between families, clinicians, schools, and relevant providers when required.

Referral Assistance

Support is provided with referrals, Medicare documentation, and administrative processes to streamline access to care.

Ongoing Follow-Up

Regular administrative follow-up helps maintain continuity of care and supports families throughout their therapy journey.

Flexible Access

Families can access support through Brisbane-based appointments or convenient online therapy services across Australia.

How do I get started?

If your family needs support, please email us using the form below or contact us , and we will guide you through the next steps and connect you with a suitable Brisbane psychologist or allied health practitioner .

You may also view our Practitioner Page and select the clinician of your choice.

Important safety note

If you are in immediate danger, experiencing severe distress, or having thoughts of harming yourself, contact emergency services or a crisis service right away. If you are concerned but not in immediate danger, please mention this when you contact us so we can prioritise an appropriate, timely response.

What is Family Therapy?

Family therapy is a collaborative approach that focuses on improving relationships and communication within the family system. Rather than viewing challenges as belonging to one individual, family therapy explores how family members interact and influence one another.

Therapy may involve parents, children, teenagers, siblings, couples, carers, grandparents, or blended family members. Sessions are tailored to the unique needs and goals of each family.

When can family therapy help?

Families seek therapy for many different reasons, including:

  • Ongoing conflict or communication difficulties • Parenting challenges • Behavioural concerns in children or teenagers • Anxiety, depression, or other mental health conditions affecting family life • Separation, divorce, or blended family adjustments • Adoption and foster care transitions • Grief, loss, or significant life changes • Relationship strain between family members

Early support can often help prevent challenges from becoming more complex over time.

Supporting Families Through Change

Modern families come in many forms, including nuclear families, single-parent households, blended families, adoptive families, foster families, and multi-generational households.

Major life transitions can affect family dynamics, emotional wellbeing, and communication patterns. Therapy provides a supportive environment where family members can develop greater understanding, strengthen relationships, and learn practical strategies for navigating change together.

Support for Adoptive Families

Adoption can bring joy, connection, and new opportunities, but it can also involve unique emotional and relational challenges for both parents and children.

Therapy may assist families in navigating adjustment periods, identity questions, attachment concerns, family communication, behavioural challenges, and transitions throughout childhood and adolescence. Support is tailored to the individual experiences of each family and child.

With appropriate support, families can learn effective ways to respond to challenges while maintaining healthy relationships and protecting their own well-being.

Supporting a Family Member Through Mental Health Challenges

When a loved one experiences mental health difficulties, the impact often extends beyond the individual. Parents, partners, siblings, carers, and other family members may experience stress, uncertainty, frustration, or emotional exhaustion while trying to provide support.

Family-focused therapy can help improve understanding, strengthen communication, and provide practical strategies that support both the individual and the wider family unit.

1 Learn About Mental Health

Develop a better understanding of symptoms, treatment options, and recovery processes.

2 Improve Communication

Build skills that support respectful, supportive, and productive conversations.

3 Set Healthy Boundaries

Learn how to balance support for a loved one while maintaining your own wellbeing.

4 Build Coping Skills

Develop practical strategies for managing stress and navigating difficult situations.

5 Access Professional Support

Connect with experienced psychologists who can guide families through complex challenges.
